description: Package versions that entered the tree inside the 7-day maturity buffer, reviewed 7 and 14 days after publication (advisories, upstream issues, release notes), and dated milestones that ride the same list. Milestones are UTC dates derived from `published`. A review is recorded under `reviews.<milestone>` as { date, outcome: clean | flagged, note }, dated the day it is written and never later; one written up to 2 days before its milestone also carries early: { reason }, and the entry's later milestone stays due. A package entry leaves the list in the change that records its clean 14-day review; a date entry stays, with its `due` review recorded as the evidence that the day was reviewed, or, while what it waits for has not happened, its `due` moves forward with a dated `refs` line naming what was read; a package entry whose version leaves the tree before that review leaves the list too, because nothing is left to review. A date entry marks a contract milestone and never reviews a patched dependency: since 2026-10-15 every patch is watched by scripts/testing/patched-dependencies-gate.mjs, which reads the registry every 6 hours in the patched-dependencies workflow (fitness #48 holds its records), so the date entry patch-storybook-nextjs-vite-10.6.3 that ADR-0037 opened left the list the day the gate landed. A date entry never schedules a dependency move either: since 2026-10-14 (ADR-0036) a non-security bump is taken in the weekly Tuesday window and a toolchain lag is legal for 30 days, so the scheduled hold entries left the list, their evidence in the pull requests that took or retired each move. Read by scripts/testing/maturity-watchlist.mjs (--check in CI, --remind in the maturity-reminder workflow).

entered.via: the root packageManager field, 2.4 days after publication

maturity.note: Reviewed 2026-10-05, six days late: the reminder workflow started on 2026-10-03 and carried no day over. OSV: nothing for 12.6.0. Upstream: pnpm 12.7.0 (2026-09-25) ships three security fixes that apply to 12.6.0 — a userAgent env placeholder in pnpm-workspace.yaml was expanded and sent to the registry; on Nix a dependency bin named like a system utility could redirect the shims and launchers; manifests inside the store, cache, state or modules directories counted as workspace projects, letting lifecycle scripts run without allowBuilds approval. 12.8.2 fixes a regression introduced in 12.6.0: pnpm run kept waiting after SIGTERM when pnpm is PID 1 in a container. 12.9.0 stops pnpm login forwarding credentials to another origin on redirect. None is reachable here today (no userAgent or storeDir configured, no Nix, the four Dockerfiles run node directly, pnpm login unused), but a package manager three security fixes behind is not kept: bump packageManager to the latest mature release in its own PR (12.8.1 from 2026-10-05T17:38Z, 12.8.2 from 2026-10-07T01:15Z, 12.9.1 from 2026-10-10T20:48Z).

early.reason: Recorded on 2026-10-05, one day before the 2026-10-06 milestone, on the Maintainer's instruction of 2026-10-05. The registry and OSV were re-checked at 2026-10-05T14:05Z, as this record was written, and are unchanged since the research: latest still 12.9.1 (modified 2026-10-03T21:10Z), no OSV entry for 12.6.0 or 12.9.1.

final.note: Researched 2026-10-05, a day before the milestone, and recorded the same day as an early review. Registry after 12.6.0: 12.7.0 (2026-09-25T10:38Z), 12.8.0 (09-28T07:34Z), 12.8.1 (09-28T17:38Z), 12.8.2 (09-30T01:15Z), 12.9.0 (10-02T22:27Z), 12.9.1 (10-03T20:48Z, latest). OSV: nothing for 12.6.0 or 12.9.1; the newest GitHub pnpm advisories (2026-09-02) cover 10.x, 11.x and 12.0.0 alphas only. Release notes: 12.7.0 carries four security fixes for 12.6.0, not three; the fourth stops hard-linking packages that run a build script into the virtual store, where the script could rewrite an injected package's source or its store copy (#15483). 12.9.0 stops pnpm login forwarding credentials on redirect; 12.8.2 fixes 12.6.0's PID-1 SIGTERM regression. None is reachable beyond the store copies of the three packages allowed to build (prisma, @prisma/engines, esbuild): no userAgent or storeDir set, no Nix, no injected workspace package, the four images run node directly, pnpm login unused. A regression in the newer releases is reachable: 12.7.0 to 12.8.2 fail pnpm install --frozen-lockfile when a workspace project the lockfile records has no directory (pnpm/pnpm#16453, fixed in 12.9.0 by #16462), and each Dockerfile runs that install with three of the four apps absent (main's admin image build at 8400ba05, run 37265374768: 96 of the lockfile's 99 importers in scope, pnpm v12.6.0). Reproduced 2026-10-05 with one of two workspace projects removed: exit 1 ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE on 12.7.0, 12.8.0, 12.8.1 and 12.8.2; exit 0 on 12.6.0, 12.9.0 and 12.9.1. 12.9.0's package also unpacks to 55 MB (12.9.1: 4.1 MB). Flagged: the packageManager bump is still owed and its target moves to 12.9.1, mature from 2026-10-10T20:48Z, not the 12.8.1 or 12.8.2 the maturity review named; its PR reads the four 'Build container image' steps, green on main while their Container Security jobs fail at Trivy. The entry stays until that bump takes 12.6.0 out of the tree.

entries.title: Is there a jscpd release whose rust/Cargo.lock carries rustix 1.1.6 or later, clearing the RUSTSEC-2026-0486 that jscpd 5.4.3 still carries?
refs: Opened 2026-11-15 by the change that moved jscpd 5.4.2 → 5.4.3 and deleted the date entry jscpd-rust-advisories, whose remove-when was met: one OSV batch over v5.4.3's rust/Cargo.lock (394 crates.io packages, read 2026-11-15T22:58Z) returns none of the seven advisories that entry watched and one other, RUSTSEC-2026-0486 (GHSA-jh2m-fhpj-3vr7) on rustix 1.1.5. On 5.4.3, check:duplicates exits 0 with 987 clones and the baseline matched, and a planted 41-line copy of apps/api/src/security/resolveClientIp.ts lines 87 to 127 fails it with exit 1 naming the new clone

RUSTSEC-2026-0486 (https://api.osv.dev/v1/vulns/RUSTSEC-2026-0486, published 2026-10-27, informational: unsound): the extended-attribute functions of rustix::fs (getxattr, lgetxattr, fgetxattr, listxattr, llistxattr, flistxattr) mark as initialized bytes that a zero-length buffer never received, undefined behavior reachable from safe code; affected >=1.0.0 <1.1.6, fixed in 1.1.6. It is a crates.io advisory inside an npm binary, so pnpm audit and the OSV npm query do not see it

Reachability, why the entry watches instead of blocking: in v5.4.3's rust/Cargo.lock rustix 1.1.5 has one parent, tempfile 3.27.0, which has two: native-tls 0.2.18 (whose normal tempfile dependency is under cfg(target_os = "macos") only) and safetensors 0.8.0, which takes tempfile ^3 with no target condition through its default std feature, and which candle-core 0.11.1 and candle-nn 0.11.1 take with default features; tempfile takes rustix under cfg(any(unix, target_os = "wasi")). So the lock holds four paths to rustix, all through cpd-semantic (jscpd → cpd-semantic → ureq 3.5.1 → native-tls → tempfile; jscpd → cpd-semantic → candle-core → safetensors → tempfile; jscpd → cpd-semantic → candle-nn → safetensors → tempfile; jscpd → cpd-semantic → candle-nn → candle-core → safetensors → tempfile), and a Linux build has three of them, the ones through safetensors, because native-tls takes tempfile on macOS only. cpd-semantic serves --semantic, which nothing here passes: package.json, .jscpd.json, scripts/testing/jscpd-baseline-gate.mjs and .github/workflows hold no `semantic`, and the gate's only jscpd invocations are its lines 117 and 126 (check:duplicates) and 167 (check:duplicates:update-baseline). The installed jscpd-linux-x64-gnu 5.4.3 binary names ureq-3.5.1, rustls-webpki-0.103.16 and safetensors-0.8.0 but no rustix or tempfile crate path; a missing getxattr string proves little, since a function that cannot panic leaves none, and whether tempfile or safetensors ever calls rustix::fs xattr functions was not read

Upstream, read 2026-11-15T22:58Z: master's rust/Cargo.lock carries rustix 1.1.6, and its newest commit touching that file is b79927a3 (2026-11-13T10:06Z, #1300), after the release; npm latest is 5.4.3 (2026-11-08T06:53:40Z), and `pnpm view jscpd time` lists no later version

The review, on the due date: read the npm registry for a jscpd release after 5.4.3 and, for each one, read rustix in its rust/Cargo.lock at the release tag and OSV-batch that lock; record whether it carries rustix 1.1.6 or later, whether it is mature (7 days after publication), and what check:duplicates and a planted clone measure on it. Plant a syntactically complete block: on 5.4.3 a 40-line copy that ends inside an unclosed function body added its lines to the scan and no clone. A release that carries rustix 1.1.6 or later is a security-tied move, taken once mature with this entry's evidence; while none exists, `due` moves to the next Tuesday window with a dated line here. The entry stays until the tree's jscpd carries rustix 1.1.6 or later, or until the advisory becomes reachable here, which is a move at once

Read 2026-11-17, the due date: npm dist-tags at 15:48Z give latest 5.4.3 (2026-11-08T06:53:40Z), and `pnpm view jscpd time` lists no later version (the registry document was last modified 2026-11-08T06:53:40Z), so there is no release whose rust/Cargo.lock could be read and the tree's jscpd 5.4.3 still carries rustix 1.1.5. package.json, .jscpd.json, scripts/testing/jscpd-baseline-gate.mjs and .github/workflows still hold no `semantic`, so the advisory stays unreachable here; `due` moved from 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-24, the next Tuesday window.

entries.title: Is there a picomatch release outside <= 4.0.7 that fixes GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf, so its entry can leave auditConfig.ignoreGhsas?
refs: Opened 2026-11-17 by the change that added GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf to auditConfig.ignoreGhsas in pnpm-workspace.yaml, by the Maintainer's decision of 2026-11-17; its row is docs/security/DEPENDENCY_AUDIT_RECORD.md §"Ignored GHSAs". The advisory (high, CVE-2026-112366, CWE-1333: denial of service through a single-branch repeated extglob pattern such as `+(*)`) covers picomatch <= 4.0.7 with no patched version; GitHub reviewed it at 2026-11-17T15:56:42Z, which turned pnpm audit red with no change in the tree. Measured that day: without the entry `pnpm audit --json` exits 1 naming this advisory and no other; with it, it exits 0 with an empty advisories map

Upstream, read 2026-11-17: npm latest is 4.0.7 (published 2026-08-24T14:36Z, the registry document's last modification), the newest 3.x and 2.x are 3.0.2 and 2.3.2 (2026-03-23), and micromatch/picomatch was last pushed 2026-10-08T04:42Z. Three candidate fixes are open with no review: #237 (master, opened 2026-10-22, "fix: CVE-2026-112366 prevent ReDoS in single-branch repeated extglobs"), #238 (master, opened 2026-10-22, "fix: literalize single-branch extglobs with a leading bare quantifier (CVE-2026-112366)") and #246 (v2, opened 2026-10-31, "[v2] Guard single-branch repeated-star extglobs against ReDoS")

Reachability, why the entry ignores instead of blocking: the lockfile holds one copy, picomatch 4.0.7; `pnpm why picomatch --prod` is empty for @apps/api and @apps/workers and reaches the portals only through build tooling (next-intl → @parcel/watcher, @sentry/nextjs → @rollup/plugin-commonjs). The trigger is the pattern, and every pattern that reaches a picomatch copy is a literal of tracked configuration or a library's own constant, never a request; the record's row holds the measurement

The review, on the due date: read `gh pr view <n> --repo micromatch/picomatch` for #237, #238 and #246 (state, merge, reviews), `pnpm view picomatch time --json` for a release after 4.0.7, and `gh api /advisories/GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf` for a patched version. A release outside <= 4.0.7 that carries the fix is a security-tied move, taken once mature (7 days after publication) or earlier as a deviation the Maintainer decides: the lockfile resolves it, the entry leaves auditConfig.ignoreGhsas, the record's row moves to the section's history, and `pnpm audit --audit-level low` verifies the tree without the entry; this entry leaves the list with that change. While none exists, `due` moves to the next Tuesday window with a dated line here. A pattern that a request, a tenant or a provider controls reaching a picomatch copy in a production process makes the advisory reachable, which is a decision at once, not a wait

entries.title: Is dompurify 3.4.18, the fix of GHSA-qm7q-q8h9-jg8q, mature, so it is taken as the dompurify security floor?
refs: Opened 2026-11-17 by the change that recorded GHSA-qm7q-q8h9-jg8q in docs/security/DEPENDENCY_AUDIT_RECORD.md §"Floor history", block `dompurify`; the floor's row is §"CVE-floor pins", `dompurify`. The advisory (medium, CWE-79 and CWE-1336, no CVE; a cure53/DOMPurify repository advisory published 2026-11-14T15:08:05Z) is a SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES bypass: template expressions reassemble when the sanitized string is parsed again, so a template engine that compiles that DOM evaluates them. It covers dompurify < 3.4.18, patched in 3.4.18; the lockfile's one copy is 3.4.17, through isomorphic-dompurify 4.7.0

Why no gate sees it, read 2026-11-17T21:29Z: GitHub's global endpoint (`gh api advisories/GHSA-qm7q-q8h9-jg8q`) answers 404, npm's bulk endpoint, which pnpm audit reads, answers {} for dompurify 3.4.17, and OSV answers 404 for the id and {} for dompurify 3.4.17, so pnpm audit is silent

Upstream, read 2026-11-17: npm latest is 3.4.18, published 2026-11-14T14:18:25Z and mature from 2026-11-21T14:18Z; isomorphic-dompurify latest is 4.7.0 (2026-11-07T06:19Z), which declares dompurify ^3.4.17, a range that admits 3.4.18

Reachability, why the entry waits for maturity instead of moving at once: the one call, apps/api/src/lib/templates/ServerTemplateEngine.ts:190, is `DOMPurify.sanitize(content)` with the default profile; no file under apps/ or packages/ sets SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES, and none of the 101 tracked package.json files declares vue or angular, the template engines the advisory's trigger compiles the output with; the record's block holds the measurement

The review, on the due date: read `pnpm view dompurify time --json` for a release after 3.4.18 and OSV for the version to take, then take 3.4.18 as the security floor: the lockfile resolves it inside isomorphic-dompurify's ^3.4.17 or, if a consumer's range does not admit it by then, an override band holds it (`"dompurify@<3.4.18": 3.4.18`); re-measure the lockfile's copies, the reachability and `pnpm audit --audit-level low`, raise the record's row to the new floor, and delete this entry with that change. Taking it before 2026-11-21T14:18Z is a deviation the Maintainer decides. A call that sets SAFE_FOR_TEMPLATES, or a template engine that compiles sanitized output, makes the advisory reachable, which is a move at once, not a wait

final.note: Reviewed 2026-11-14, four days after the 2026-11-10 milestone (reminder #864). Registry, read 2026-11-14T00:21Z: latest is 14.0.6 (2026-11-12T12:02:26Z, mature from 2026-11-19T12:02Z); 14.0.3 (2026-10-28T04:08Z) and 14.0.4 (2026-11-06T03:47Z) are mature, 14.0.5 (2026-11-11T18:20Z) is not; none of 14.0.2 to 14.0.6 is deprecated. Advisories: isaacs/node-glob published the repository advisory GHSA-qxr8-q827-836c on 2026-11-12T12:04:05Z (low; CWE-400, CWE-405, CWE-770; glob >=13.0.5 <=14.0.5, patched 14.0.6): the Ignore class builds its minimatch options without braceExpandMax, so an ignore pattern may expand to minimatch's default of 100,000 rows where a pattern is held to 10,000; 14.0.6's one code commit, 17cb2074, passes the limit to it. GitHub's global database (affects=glob@14.0.2) and OSV, read 00:21Z, list nothing for 14.0.2 to 14.0.6, so pnpm audit cannot see it, and main's Security Audit passed at 2026-11-13T23:19Z. Upstream, opened since 2026-10-27: node-glob#664 (closed, a 13.x cancellation backport) and pull request #665 (closed, a trailing **), neither a security report. Lockfile: one copy, 14.0.2, under rimraf 5.0.10, @sentry/bundler-plugins 10.76.2 and @joshwooding/vite-plugin-react-docgen-typescript 0.7.0; no manifest or source module of apps, packages, infra or scripts declares or imports glob. Reachability, as DEPENDENCY_AUDIT_RECORD.md row `glob` reads: gaxios never calls rimraf, and Sentry's globFiles and the Storybook docgen plugin pass ignore patterns from build configuration, never request input. Works here: on main af93f0fa, CI run 43526148952 (push, 2026-11-13T23:18Z, success) passed Build Check, Storybook Stories, Lint and Format Check, Frontend Tests, Package Tests, both Test Suite shards and Integration Tests; Production CI/CD 43526148953 passed Test and Build and the four Container Security jobs; Architectural Fitness Functions 43526149011 passed. Flagged, not clean: 14.0.2 carries an advisory that 14.0.6 fixes, so raising the floor (the override `glob@<14.0.2` in pnpm-workspace.yaml and its row in the audit record) is owed in its own change, once 14.0.6 is mature on 2026-11-19T12:02Z or earlier as a security-tied deviation the Maintainer decides; the entry stays until that change takes 14.0.2 out of the tree.

final.note: Reviewed 2026-11-14, four days after the 2026-11-10 milestone (reminder #865). Advisories: isaacs/minimatch published three repository advisories after the 7-day review. GHSA-cf2h-pxjq-68xw (2026-11-10T23:05:21Z, medium, CWE-407, >=11.0.0 <=11.0.6, patched 11.0.7): mergeRows compiles a pattern of many wildcard-only parts in quadratic time. GHSA-c859-jr93-m5j4 (2026-11-11T09:51:30Z, medium, CWE-116, >=7.4.0 <=11.0.7, patched 11.0.8): escape() leaves a leading ! or #, its escaped backslash collapses under brace expansion, and with windowsPathsNoEscape and magicalBraces its brace classes expand, so its output matches more or less than the literal. GHSA-hqmv-qgp3-jx75 (2026-11-11T09:50:24Z, medium, >=11.0.3 <=11.0.7) names 11.0.1 a negative control. The first two cover 11.0.1, and neither covers the 3.1.5 copy of the Blocked floor. GitHub's global database (affects=minimatch@11.0.1) and OSV, read 00:21Z, list nothing for 11.0.1 to 11.0.8, so pnpm audit cannot see them, and main's Security Audit passed at 2026-11-13T23:19Z. 11.0.5 also bounds the cells of the glob split pass and throws when a **/.. expansion goes over the limit (73f0e1b1, 2d5578ba), with no advisory of its own. Upstream issues opened since 2026-10-27, beside the advisories: #333 (closed, the CVE of GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249), #338 (closed, the cost of the cache key), #340 (open, unescape skips adjacent bracket escapes) and #342 (closed, a CVE request for GHSA-hqmv-qgp3-jx75). Works here: on main af93f0fa, CI run 43526148952 (push, 2026-11-13T23:18Z, success) passed Lint and Format Check, Build Check, Storybook Stories, Package Tests and both Test Suite shards; Architectural Fitness Functions 43526149011 and Production CI/CD 43526148953 passed.
